title: Households cluster at Çatalhöyük
summary: The eastern mound at Çatalhöyük preserves successive levels of closely packed houses. Roof access, paintings and household features document a distinctive form of settled community life in Neolithic Anatolia.

claims.text: The eastern mound at Çatalhöyük preserves successive levels of closely packed houses. Roof access, paintings and household features document a distinctive form of settled community life in Neolithic Anatolia.
Eastern mound occupation only; the western mound continued into a later phase.

Dense settlement need not resemble later street-based cities. This record invites comparison of household organization and shared space, while separating the eastern mound’s chronology from the later western settlement.
